rulings.challenge_claim: The row's stated internal-cohesion ground -- one first-person divine speaker running from Isa.29.2 through Isa.29.8 -- is contradicted by the bytes, and an accent-stripped-tier of-hosts formula straddles the row's own front seam undisclosed.
rulings.grounds: Re-derived from source bytes; both limbs hold and the challenge verifies its OBJECTS, not merely its digits. First-person divine forms in this span are confined to two verses: וַהֲצִיק֖וֹתִי at oshb:Isa.29.2 and וְחָנִ֥יתִי with וְצַרְתִּ֤י at oshb:Isa.29.3 (byte tier). oshb:Isa.29.4 is second-person feminine address, וְשָׁפַלְתְּ֙ (byte tier), not divine self-reference; a person-form scan of oshb:Isa.29.5-Isa.29.8 returns no first-person verb or suffix anywhere; and oshb:Isa.29.6 names the deity in the third person, מֵעִ֨ם יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ תִּפָּקֵ֔ד (byte tier). The row's device_notes ground -- the reversal read as continuing the same first-person divine speaker -- is byte-false as written. The second limb verifies on an independent re-sweep and is honestly tiered: the of-hosts run מֵעִ֨ם יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ תִּפָּקֵ֔ד is byte-unique to oshb:Isa.29.6 (1 verse), meets מֵעִ֛ם יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת at oshb:Isa.28.29 only at accent-stripped tier, and stands at exactly 3 verses book-wide at that tier (oshb:Isa.8.18, oshb:Isa.28.29, oshb:Isa.29.6). oshb:Isa.28.29 is the verse immediately before the row's front seam, so the recurrence straddles it and owes disclosure under the cross-seam rule. The boundary is untouched: ה֚וֹי is verse-initial at oshb:Isa.29.1 (byte tier, tier-1 woe onset), and the tier-3 setumah at Isa.28.29 and Isa.29.8 match the single-witness inventory under the correct, unconflated type.
rulings.remedy: Author wave, two edits in one pass. (1) device_notes: strike the clause resting the Isa.29.5 hold on the same first-person divine speaker and re-ground it on what the bytes carry -- no fresh frame onset, no vocative and no addressee shift into Isa.29.5-Isa.29.8, plus the name-chain אֲרִיאֵ֑ל, which stands at exactly 3 verses book-wide at consonantal-skeleton tier (oshb:Isa.29.1, oshb:Isa.29.2, oshb:Isa.29.7; 5 token occurrences) and so spans the very division the row argues against, together with the byte-identical run כָּל הַגּוֹיִ֔ם הַצֹּבְאִ֖ים עַל shared by oshb:Isa.29.7 and oshb:Isa.29.8 (byte tier, exactly 2 verses book-wide). (2) boundary_rationale or device_notes: add a one-clause cross-seam disclosure naming the of-hosts recurrence at accent-stripped tier with its 3-verse book-wide digit and its seam-adjacent oshb:Isa.28.29 site; add oshb:Isa.28.29 and oshb:Isa.29.6 to boundary_evidence_refs. Cure test -- the test that killed the original: a person-form scan of oshb:Isa.29.5-Isa.29.8 must return zero first-person verb or suffix forms without contradicting any sentence the row states, and no replacement cohesion ground may be located wholly inside Isa.29.5-Isa.29.8.

rulings.challenge_claim: OL: the opener is labelled a vocative onset where the bytes carry imperatives with no vocative element; the non-dividing argument at Isa.29.13 rests on a constant addressee the bytes contradict; the frame's speaker class is unnamed; and the scroll catchword crosses the rear seam undisclosed. LF: strongest_rejected_alternative names isolating the sealed-book simile rather than the live rival of a fresh unit opening at Isa.29.13's own speech-frame.
rulings.grounds: Both items are upheld. They are DISTINCT defects that converge on ONE site, oshb:Isa.29.13, and take one cure. OL limb 1, byte-verified: oshb:Isa.29.9 opens הִתְמַהְמְה֣וּ וּתְמָ֔הוּ הִשְׁתַּֽעַשְׁע֖וּ וָשֹׁ֑עוּ (byte tier) -- four second-person plural imperative forms, with no vocative particle and no addressee noun anywhere in the verse. The row's own boundary_rationale calls this a doubled imperative in one clause and a fresh vocative onset in the next, and its observed_substrate_signals key records the vocative reading; the bytes carry an imperative onset. OL limb 2, byte-verified: second-person plural marking runs to oshb:Isa.29.11 -- עֲלֵיכֶ֤ם and עֵֽינֵיכֶ֑ם at oshb:Isa.29.10, לָכֶ֜ם at oshb:Isa.29.11 (byte tier) -- and stops there. oshb:Isa.29.13 names its object in the third person, הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֔ה, while speaking as the deity, כִּבְּד֔וּנִי and מִמֶּ֑נִּי (byte tier), and oshb:Isa.29.14 continues first-person with הִנְנִ֥י (byte tier). The addressee does not stay constant, so the row's stated non-dividing ground is byte-false. OL limb 3 is the weakest and I discount it to register level rather than defect level: the frame is וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲדֹנָ֗י (byte tier) and the row's signal key already records the vayomer-adonai form. The bare-adonai role-split this book carries (51 verses) is live in the narrative zone, not at oshb:Isa.29.13, where first-person divine indictment follows in the same verse. It carries no severity here. OL limb 4, byte-verified and load-bearing: the scroll noun stands at oshb:Isa.29.11 and as סֵֽפֶר at oshb:Isa.29.12, both inside the span, and recurs at דִּבְרֵי סֵ֑פֶר at oshb:Isa.29.18, beyond the rear seam -- exactly 4 verses at consonantal-skeleton tier in chapters 28-31 (oshb:Isa.29.11, oshb:Isa.29.12, oshb:Isa.29.18, oshb:Isa.30.8) out of 20 book-wide. It straddles the row's own rear seam undisclosed. LF is correct and independent: the row's boundary_rationale expressly argues against a division at Isa.29.13, which makes that the rival it actually weighed, yet strongest_rejected_alternative names the sealed-book simile instead -- and the tier-3 setumah inside that simile falls at Isa.29.12, mid-simile (single-witness, verified against the inventory), so the named rival has no edge to stand on. Same defect? No. OL kills the REASON given at Isa.29.13; LF shows the RIVAL at Isa.29.13 was never promoted. One site, two findings, one cure.
rulings.remedy: Author wave, one coordinated edit. (1) observed_substrate_signals: replace the vocative-onset key with the imperative-onset key of the same signal family, and re-cut the boundary_rationale onset sentence to say imperative onset (four forms) rather than vocative onset. This is a driver-label correction, so its dependent fields re-open: re-check observed_substrate_signals as a whole, unit_type, confidence and strongest_rejected_alternative against the corrected driver. (2) boundary_rationale: replace the constant-addressee clause with the byte-true ground for holding Isa.29.13-Isa.29.14 in -- the indictment object continues from the blinded people of Isa.29.9-Isa.29.12 while the person-marking turns, and no fresh frame opens between them -- and name the divine speaker class on the frame explicitly. (3) strongest_rejected_alternative: replace the sealed-book-simile rival with the Isa.29.13 speech-frame rival, one sentence, with the optional second sentence carrying the rival disclosure. (4) Add the rear-seam catchword disclosure with its scoped tier and digit, and add oshb:Isa.29.9, oshb:Isa.29.10 and oshb:Isa.29.18 to boundary_evidence_refs. ORCHESTRATOR NOTE: item (4) is one half of a SEAM PAIR -- the identical catchword crossing is charged from the other side on P08-006's front seam at the same Isa.29.14|Isa.29.15 edge. Under seam-pair law the two are ONE edit and must be cured together with matching tier label and digit, not separately. Cure test: no sentence may assert a constant addressee across Isa.29.12|Isa.29.13; a person-form scan must show second-person plural marking ending at oshb:Isa.29.11; the onset label must match the forms present in oshb:Isa.29.9; and the catchword claim must name consonantal-skeleton tier with its scope.

rulings.challenge_claim: The row's divine-title cohesion evidence rests on one in-span occurrence argued from the English rendering, and the scroll catchword crossing its front seam is undisclosed; the potter-and-clay catchword claim is byte-true and correctly tiered.
rulings.grounds: The defects are real and byte-confirmed, but the severity is understated and the framing of the title defect is not the sharpest available. Verified: the title-construct occurs in this span at exactly ONE site, בִּקְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל at oshb:Isa.29.19 (byte tier). The book carries 25 title verses and the chapters-28-31 members are Isa.29.19, Isa.30.11, Isa.30.12, Isa.30.15, Isa.31.1, so every other link of the chain lies outside the span. The row carries no oshb: ref, no pointed form and no tier for this claim -- it is argued from an English quotation alone, on a signal the row DECLARES in observed_substrate_signals. That is an engagement-class breach on a boundary-relevant Hebrew claim, not a texture aside. Sharper than the challenge states: the defect is not only that one occurrence cannot show one voice running through the row, it is WHERE that occurrence sits. oshb:Isa.29.19 lies wholly inside the promise half, while the rival the row is arguing against would cut at Isa.29.16|Isa.29.17; a single site on one side of the contested internal division cannot corroborate cohesion across it. The evidence is located where it cannot do the work claimed. Verified: the front-seam catchword crossing holds -- the scroll noun at oshb:Isa.29.11 and oshb:Isa.29.12 recurs inside this span at דִּבְרֵי סֵ֑פֶר at oshb:Isa.29.18 (4 verses at consonantal-skeleton tier in chapters 28-31; 20 book-wide), undisclosed. Credited items verify exactly: ה֛וֹי is verse-initial at oshb:Isa.29.15 (byte tier, tier-1 woe onset); and כִּֽי at oshb:Isa.29.16 against יֵחָשֵֽׁב at oshb:Isa.29.17 are byte-distinct and meet at consonantal-skeleton tier only, attested at exactly 5 verses book-wide at that tier (oshb:Isa.10.7, oshb:Isa.13.17, oshb:Isa.29.16, oshb:Isa.29.17, oshb:Isa.32.15), the sole adjacent pair among them. The row tiers that honestly and it is the row's real cohesion driver. SEVERITY REFINED low to medium. A byte-false inference drawn on a declared substrate signal with zero Hebrew engagement is the same defect class that drew medium on the neighbouring rows in this cluster, and the low band under-prices it. The boundary itself is not endangered, which is why it does not rise above medium.
rulings.remedy: Author wave. (1) boundary_rationale: rewrite the title sentence to state exactly what the bytes carry -- a single in-span title site at oshb:Isa.29.19, spliced pointed with its tier named -- and delete the inference that it shows one voice running through the row. If a cohesion ground is still wanted across the Isa.29.16|Isa.29.17 division, use the shared-verb bridge the row already tiers honestly, which is the only evidence that actually spans it. Add oshb:Isa.29.19 to boundary_evidence_refs. (2) Add the front-seam catchword disclosure with its scoped consonantal-skeleton digit. ORCHESTRATOR NOTE: this is the OTHER half of the seam pair charged on P08-005's rear seam at the same Isa.29.14|Isa.29.15 edge -- ONE edit, matching wording, cured together. (3) If the title survives in observed_substrate_signals it must be evidenced from pointed bytes with a named tier; otherwise drop the key, which re-opens unit_type and confidence as dependent fields. Cure test: no sentence may claim cohesion across Isa.29.16|Isa.29.17 from evidence attested only on one side of it, and every declared substrate signal in the row must have at least one pointed splice with a named tier behind it.

rulings.challenge_claim: A clause repeated at consonantal-skeleton tier across the row's own rear seam is left undisclosed while the row records high confidence, and the rival reading is stated without its byte grounds.
rulings.grounds: Verified from bytes, and the challenge's tier discrimination is exactly right -- the sharpest item in the cluster. The run עַל עַ֖ם לֹא יוֹעִ֣ילוּ stands at oshb:Isa.30.5 (byte tier) followed by לָ֑מוֹ, and oshb:Isa.30.6 ends on עַל עַ֖ם לֹ֥א יוֹעִֽילוּ (byte tier). Re-swept independently at all three tiers, the two meet at consonantal-skeleton tier and at NO higher tier, and at that tier the clause is attested in exactly 2 verses book-wide, oshb:Isa.30.5 and oshb:Isa.30.6. The accent-stripped tier separates them (1 verse) because the second site retains meteg where the first carries cantillation -- the challenge's tier call survives the check. Its count-object is the shared run, not the longer oshb:Isa.30.5 clause it also quotes; the quoted clause and the swept string differ, which is a presentation looseness in the challenge and not a count-object error. The Egypt naming crosses the same seam and verifies: מִצְרַ֖יִם and its attested byform spellings stand at oshb:Isa.30.2 and oshb:Isa.30.3 inside the span and at oshb:Isa.30.7 beyond it -- 40 verses book-wide at consonantal-skeleton tier, in chapters 28-31 at Isa.30.2, Isa.30.3, Isa.30.7, Isa.31.1, Isa.31.3. It is the weaker of the two because it skips the header verse itself. The row records HIGH confidence and its strongest_rejected_alternative names the extend-through-Isa.30.7 rival in a bare sentence with no byte ground at all, so the strongest counter-evidence to its own cut appears nowhere in the row. Under the cross-seam rule an undisclosed device straddling the row's own seam argues continuity against it, and here that lands on the top confidence band. Credited and verified: ה֣וֹי בָּנִ֤ים סֽוֹרְרִים֙ נְאֻם יְהוָ֔ה is verse-initial at oshb:Isa.30.1 (byte tier), a woe onset with the postpositive signature attached; the tier-3 setumah at Isa.30.5 matches the single-witness inventory under the correct type; and the row's variant-note slicing statement is accurate.
rulings.remedy: Author wave. (1) strongest_rejected_alternative: re-cut so the rival carries its actual textual ground -- the clause repeated across Isa.30.5|Isa.30.6, named at consonantal-skeleton tier with its 2-verse book-wide digit -- instead of a bare assertion, using the sanctioned optional second sentence for the rival disclosure. (2) Add the cross-seam disclosure to boundary_rationale or device_notes with the tier named, and add oshb:Isa.30.5 and oshb:Isa.30.6 to boundary_evidence_refs. (3) confidence: re-decide after the disclosure lands. High is not defensible while the strongest counter-evidence to the cut is absent from the row; the cut itself stands on the verse-initial header at oshb:Isa.30.6, so it is the band that moves, not the span -- this remedy proposes no boundary change. ORCHESTRATOR NOTE: one half of a SEAM PAIR with P08-009 at the same Isa.30.5|Isa.30.6 edge -- ONE edit, matching wording and matching tier label on both rows. Cure test -- the test that killed the original: a book-wide sweep of the shared run at all three tiers must appear in the row with the skeleton tier named and the 2-verse digit stated, and no sentence may describe the rival as merely thematic.

rulings.challenge_claim: The row cuts correctly on a verse-initial burden header but describes the rival as thematic when the bytes repeat a clause across that seam, understating the counter-weight on a low-band hold.
rulings.grounds: The defect is real and byte-confirmed, but the severity is one band too high for this row. Verified: the same skeleton-tier repetition adjudicated on P08-008 crosses this row's FRONT seam -- עַל עַ֖ם לֹא יוֹעִ֣ילוּ at oshb:Isa.30.5 against עַל עַ֖ם לֹ֥א יוֹעִֽילוּ closing oshb:Isa.30.6 (both byte tier as spliced), meeting only at consonantal-skeleton tier, exactly 2 verses book-wide. The row's strongest_rejected_alternative rests the rival on shared Egypt-reliance subject-matter and the absence of an addressee shift; the bytes give lexical repetition, a materially higher grade of counter-evidence than theme. The challenge's finding is correct. Also verified, all credited to the row: מַשָּׂ֖א בַּהֲמ֣וֹת נֶ֑גֶב is verse-initial at oshb:Isa.30.6 (byte tier) and is the construct-header form, correctly kept apart from the burden common noun וְכֹ֖בֶד at oshb:Isa.30.27. The skeleton is attested at 15 verses book-wide of which exactly 10 are verse-initial headers, so the row's 10-header digit and the challenge's role-split both check out against a contiguous-substring sweep that would otherwise blend the three roles. The rear-seam opener עַתָּ֗ה בּ֣וֹא at oshb:Isa.30.8 is unique in the book (1 verse at consonantal-skeleton tier), and the tier-3 setumah at Isa.30.5 matches the single-witness inventory. SEVERITY REFINED medium to low, on the row's own exposure. Unlike its seam partner this row does NOT record high confidence: it is held at medium_low, it names the header-inside-woe-zone tension in device_notes rather than suppressing it, and it discloses the continuity rival in substance. What is wrong is the GRADE assigned to that rival, not its absence. A disclosure that exists but understates its evidentiary tier on an already-hedged low-band row is a prose-completeness defect, not a position-endangering one -- and the asymmetry with P08-008, where the identical device is absent entirely at the top band, is the calibration this pair needs.
rulings.remedy: Author wave, and this is the SAME EDIT as the P08-008 remedy, not a second one -- seam-pair law. In strongest_rejected_alternative, replace the thematic ground with the textual one: the closing clause of the header verse repeats the clause the preceding verse turns on, at consonantal-skeleton tier, attested in exactly 2 verses book-wide. Keep the formal-header ground for the cut, which is untouched; no boundary change is proposed. Add oshb:Isa.30.5 to boundary_evidence_refs. Cure test: the rival sentence must name a tier and carry a digit, and the same tier label and digit must appear on both rows of the pair.

rulings.challenge_claim: OL: the messenger-frame and divine-title signals are asserted from the English rendering, without a pointed form, a tier or a named frame owner -- at the one site in the span where the frame is owned by a non-adjacent title. LF: the row folds the koh-amar citations into the unit's texture without stating which speech-frame class they carry, leaving the frame identification implicit in the adjacent title.
rulings.grounds: The SAME defect from both lenses -- the frame class is never named -- with OL strictly the broader statement of it. Adjudicated as one, at OL's severity, which subsumes LF's. Verified from bytes: the two frames are לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ קְד֣וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל at oshb:Isa.30.12 and כִּ֣י כֹֽה אָמַר֩ אֲדֹנָ֨י יְהוִ֜ה קְד֣וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל at oshb:Isa.30.15 (byte tier), both divine. The row quotes neither in Hebrew: its boundary_evidence_refs carry oshb:Isa.30.8 alone, every other cited site being a web: ref, so two declared substrate signals -- the messenger-formula key and the divine-title key -- rest on English quotations with no pointed form and no tier. OL's sharpest point verifies, and is why this outranks LF's low band: at oshb:Isa.30.12 the frame's owner IS the title, with no adjacent divine name in the clause -- precisely the configuration this book's messenger-formula census is role-split to catch, since an unnamed owner there cannot be checked at all, whereas at oshb:Isa.30.15 the divine name stands inside the frame itself. LF's inference that the adjacent title marks the class is right in result but is exactly the implicit reasoning the naming rule exists to forbid. The title digit verifies: the three in-span sites are אֶת קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל at oshb:Isa.30.11 and the title standing inside each of the two frames (byte tier) -- correct against the 25-verse book-wide inventory, whose chapters-28-31 members are Isa.29.19, Isa.30.11, Isa.30.12, Isa.30.15, Isa.31.1. OL's third observation verifies and is correctly kept below severity: בּ֣וֹא כָתְבָ֥הּ at oshb:Isa.30.8 (byte tier) is second-person masculine SINGULAR against the plural marking around it, so the singular-versus-plural contrast the row's onset rests on is byte-supported, but the verse names no addressee, so the row's assignment of the commission to the prophet is an inference the cited verse does not carry. Credited: the opener עַתָּ֗ה בּ֣וֹא is unique in the book (1 verse at consonantal-skeleton tier), and both in-span marked divisions are disclosed under the correct, unconflated types -- a setumah at Isa.30.11 and a petuchah at Isa.30.14 -- matching the single-witness inventory.
rulings.remedy: Author wave, one pass. (1) boundary_rationale: splice both frames pointed from source with their oshb: refs and name the tier, and state the frame class explicitly as divine for each -- at oshb:Isa.30.12 naming the title AS the frame owner, since no adjacent divine name stands there. (2) Splice the title at oshb:Isa.30.11 pointed with its tier rather than quoting three English renderings; or demote the title to device_notes as texture and drop its substrate-signal key, which then re-opens unit_type and confidence as dependent fields. (3) Add oshb:Isa.30.11, oshb:Isa.30.12 and oshb:Isa.30.15 to boundary_evidence_refs. (4) Soften the prophet-referent assertion at oshb:Isa.30.8 to what the verse carries -- a second-person singular commission against the surrounding plural, referent not named in the verse. No boundary change is proposed. Cure test -- the test that killed the original: every declared substrate signal in the row must be traceable to a pointed splice with a named tier and an oshb: ref, and no messenger-formula citation may stand without naming whose frame it is.

rulings.challenge_claim: The row's opener is a consequence connector rather than a temporal turn, and the speaking voice changes at the front seam instead of continuing -- so both stated grounds fail even though the boundary itself is sound; and the in-span paseq at Isa.30.25 is omitted while the row engages the marked-division layer.
rulings.grounds: Both stated grounds are byte-false and the disclosure gap is real; the challenge's conclusion -- the boundary is better supported than the row argues -- also verifies. Ground one: oshb:Isa.30.18 opens וְלָכֵ֞ן יְחַכֶּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ לַֽחֲנַנְכֶ֔ם (byte tier) and carries the same particle a second time later in the verse, with no temporal element anywhere in it. Re-swept independently and word-bound to guard against substring bleed, the bare particle stands at exactly 25 verses book-wide at consonantal-skeleton tier -- 23 bare plus 2 with the conjunction, the contiguous-substring and word-bound digits agreeing -- and within chapters 29-30 at Isa.29.14, Isa.29.22, Isa.30.7, Isa.30.12, Isa.30.13 and Isa.30.18, the same form לָכֵ֗ן that opens the indictment frame at oshb:Isa.30.12. It is this book's consequence connector; the row's temporal-turn label is byte-false. Ground two: the verses the row turns from are divine speech under the frame at oshb:Isa.30.15 addressing second-person plural -- גְּבֽוּרַתְכֶ֑ם and אֲבִיתֶֽם at oshb:Isa.30.15, תָּנֻ֑סוּ and נוֹתַרְתֶּ֗ם at oshb:Isa.30.17 (byte tier) -- while oshb:Isa.30.18 names the deity in the third person. The speaking voice does change at the front seam, so the same-voice ground fails. REFINEMENT the challenge does not supply and the cure needs: the ADDRESSEE does continue across that seam, oshb:Isa.30.18's second-person plural object suffixes answering the second-person plural of oshb:Isa.30.15 and oshb:Isa.30.17 (byte tier). The continuity the row was reaching for exists; it was attached to the wrong grammatical category. That converts the finding from a wholesale loss of ground into a correctable restatement, and it is what the replacement warrant should rest on. Disclosure gap verified: a paseq seg stands at Isa.30.25, inside the span, and is the only paseq in chapters 29-30 (the next is Isa.31.4). The row engages the marked-division layer at Isa.30.18 and Isa.30.26 -- both setumah, both matching the single-witness inventory under the correct type -- and omits it. The machine arms do not catch this, which is why it needs the model pass; the neighbouring rows in this corpus do disclose their in-span paseq as presence-only, so the row is asymmetric with its own corpus.
rulings.remedy: Author wave. (1) boundary_rationale: replace the fresh-temporal-turn label with the consequence-connector reading, naming the particle's tier and its digit, and noting it is the same connector that opens the indictment frame earlier in the chapter. (2) Replace the same-speaking-voice ground with the byte-true one: the speaker turns from divine first-person speech to third-person report while the second-person plural ADDRESSEE continues unbroken across the seam -- that is the continuity the unit actually has. (3) Add the in-span paseq disclosure as presence only, single-witness, with no position claim. (4) Add oshb:Isa.30.15, oshb:Isa.30.17 and the paseq site to boundary_evidence_refs. (5) observed_substrate_signals: the reversal-onset key is a driver label the corrected reading changes; re-check it, and with it unit_type, confidence and strongest_rejected_alternative. No boundary change is proposed -- the challenge and this ruling both find the cut better supported than the row argues. Cure test -- the test that killed the original: the row must contain no temporal claim about oshb:Isa.30.18 and no same-speaker claim across Isa.30.17|Isa.30.18; a person-form scan must place the speaker change at that seam and the addressee continuity across it; and a span-relevant disclosure sweep of the row must return every marked division AND the paseq site with nothing left over.

rulings.challenge_claim: The row's apparatus work inside its own span is asymmetric -- it engages one of the two variant-note verses it covers, attributes the segment marks to the wrong witness, and leaves a two-site catchword hooking across its rear edge undisclosed.
rulings.grounds: Two of the three limbs verify; the middle limb is REFUTED on the bytes and on the campaign's own ref contract, and with it removed the severity does not hold. UPHELD, limb 1: the variant-note inventory places notes at exactly two verses inside this span, oshb:Isa.30.32 and oshb:Isa.30.33. The row engages only the second, and engages it actively -- it makes a positional slicing claim there, which verifies: the doubled pair גַּם הוא הִ֛יא stands early in oshb:Isa.30.33, well ahead of the verse-final clause the row quotes. The first note, staged the same way as נִלְחַם בה בָּֽם at oshb:Isa.30.32 with its unpointed member at skeleton grade, is nowhere disclosed.
